title: Customer strata batch & cache recommendation wizard with safe apply/rollback
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a wizard-style automation that generates per-customer and per-route batching + caching recommendations (batch window, target batch size, KV cache TTL, prefix caching allowlist/denylist) and can apply them safely with dry-run, canary, and automated rollback. The goal is measurable unit-cost improvements for each customer segment without violating latency SLOs or correctness. This work ties into the segmentation and tier controls effort: recommendations must respect customer tiers, explicit allowlists/denylists, and route-level overrides. The wizard will produce a policy bundle that can be previewed in Console and applied via an opt-in safe apply flow that supports incremental rollouts and automatic rollback based on defined regression thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: Wizard generates recommendations per-customer and per-route based on recent 14-day telemetry (median and p95 latency, tokens/request, cache hit rate).
Recommendations include concrete values: batching_window_ms, target_batch_tokens, kv_cache_ttl_seconds, allowlist_routes, denylist_routes, and priority tier mapping.

Safe apply flow supports: dry-run (simulation), canary (config applied to 1% of traffic), ramp (1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%), and automatic rollback when: +p95 latency > baseline + 100ms OR token-cost reduction < 2% for a tier for 24h.
Console shows diff of current vs recommended policy and a predicted cost delta using our cost model (tokens, kernel utilization).
End-to-end test and staging rollout exercised: non-prod environment sees identical config semantics and simulated telemetry before prod canary.
technical_notes: Segmentation: build feature vector per-customer (avg tokens/req, request rate, median latency, recent KV hit rate, model family) and map to strata: free/standard/enterprise/custom-tier.

Recommendation engine: rule-based baseline + greedy tuner that simulates batching impact on latency using our latency model (seq_len distribution + kernel profile). Use conservative defaults for tiers with high p95 sensitivity.
Allowlist/denylist precedence: explicit denylist on a customer-route pair must always override recommendations. Tier-wide policies are default unless per-customer override exists.

Safe apply: implement a config-controller that supports rollout stages, monitors defined metrics, and triggers automatic rollback using circuit-breaker semantics. Persist audit log of each apply and rollback event for compliance.
Storage: policy bundles stored as signed YAML in CustomerConfig service (existing API). Ensure immutability of applied bundle versions for traceability.
Backwards compatibility: zero-touch defaults must be preserved so applying a recommendation to a customer with no prior policies does not change behavior until canary/ramp completes.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Dry-run): run recommendation engine against 100 customers in staging and emit predicted cost delta. No config applied.
Phase 1 (Internal Canary): apply to internal test tenants (redwood-test-*) at 1% traffic split; monitor 48h.
Phase 2 (Customer Canary): pick 10 low-risk customers across tiers at 5-10% traffic; collect real telemetry for 72h.
Phase 3 (Ramp): automated ramp if thresholds pass: 10% -> 50% -> 100% over configurable windows.
Phase 4 (Full): policy becomes default for tier; schedule re-evaluation every 14 days and automatic decay if cost savings fall below threshold for 30 days.
Rollback: immediate rollback if circuit-breaker fires (latency regression, error-rate increase, or customer complaint label).
monitoring: Compute baseline per-customer: median latency, p95 latency, error rate, tokens/request, cost/1M tokens.
Primary rollback triggers: p95_latency > baseline + 100ms OR error_rate increase > 0.5% absolute OR cost regression (no cost reduction) after 24h.
Secondary signals: KV cache hit rate drop > 10% absolute, model throughput drop > 15%.
Dashboards: per-policy diff dashboard in Console (tokens saved, delta latency, cache hit rate, affected routes/customers).
Alerts: automated Slack + PagerDuty for SRE on critical regressions during canary phases.
